title: Observability ingest mesh: tenant-aware structured log sampler & compact-encoding proxy
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a lightweight ingest mesh that sits in front of our log aggregation layer (Loki/Elasticsearch) to: 1) accept structured log events from services via a gRPC/HTTP multiplexer, 2) apply tenant-aware adaptive sampling and rate-limiting, 3) encode/serialize events using a compact binary format (CBOR/protobuf) with optional compression to reduce egress and storage cost, and 4) emit enriched, idempotent records with stable correlation IDs for downstream joinability. This is intended to replace parts of the current Fluentd/Logstash fleet for high-volume tenants and provide a programmable policy layer for rollout and throttling.
acceptance_criteria: Ingress proxy accepts HTTP JSON and gRPC protobuf payloads and normalizes to internal compact schema
Per-tenant sampling policy supports probabilistic sampling and reservoir sampling fallback
Proxy exposes per-tenant meter: accepted, sampled_out, rate_limited, dropped, and avg_ingest_latency
End-to-end ingestion latency (proxy -> Loki write) P99 < 200ms for typical request size under load test profile
Compact encoding reduces average payload size by >=2.5x vs raw JSON in our sample corpus
No loss of correlation IDs: original request-id and trace-id preserved and surfaced as stable fields
Canary rollout to 3 beta tenants without increased error budget and with observability enabled
implementation_notes: Ingress protocol: single binary that supports HTTP/1.1 JSON and HTTP/2 gRPC; prefer gRPC for internal services for higher compression efficiency

Serialization: primary wire format = CBOR; fallback protobuf for typed clients. CBOR chosen for schema-flexible structured logs and small size. All records include a minimal header with tenant_id, event_ts, sequence_hint, correlation_ids

Sampling: tenant policy config stored in Config DB. Default: adaptive probabilistic sampling tuned by recent QPS and recent error rate. For short bursty traces use reservoir sampling window of 30s to capture head events.

Rate limits: hierarchical token buckets (global -> tenant -> stream). Token refill tuned by dedicated capacity tiers (free vs reserved). On hard limit, respond 429 + Retry-After and emit telemetry events to account-service for quota enforcement
Dedup/Idempotency: compute stable content hash (+ sequence_hint) to drop duplicates downstream within a 5m window using a small LRU cache per shard
Backpressure & retries: use http-graceful-retry for upstream writes. For persistent upstream failures route to cold-store (S3) with manifest for later rehydration to Loki
Security: mutual TLS for internal gRPC; tenant authentication via signed JWT / mTLS cert SAN check. KMS integration required for rehydration manifests (encrypt at rest)
Operational metrics: per-tenant histograms for ingest latency, counters for sampled/dropped/accepted, gauge for compressed_bytes_saved, and tracing spans emitted for proxy internal steps

Trade-offs considered: CBOR reduces size but requires encoder/decoder support in clients; we will provide language SDKs for node/go/python to ease adoption. Reservoir sampling captures spikes but can bias rare-event capture; acceptance criteria includes evaluation on known anomaly datasets.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - dev & e2e: local dev harness + synthetic log generator that mirrors production 95th percentile distributions (complete)
Phase 1 - internal canary: roll proxy to internal infra + platform teams (2 weeks), gather telemetry and adjust token buckets
Phase 2 - external beta: enable for 3 paid tenants with monitoring dashboards and alerting; run 2-week observation window
Phase 3 - gradual ramp: enable ingress-mesh as opt-in 'compact path' for high-throughput tenants with config flags; monitor drop rates and latency
Phase 4 - default switch: once stable and cost targets met, promote mesh to default path and decommission replaced Fluentd shards over 6 weeks
risks: Client rollout friction: older SDKs won't support CBOR/protobuf and will fallback to JSON -> higher CPU/latency
Sampling bias: naive sampling could drop rare but important errors — need test-suite of labeled anomalies
Stateful dedup caches increase memory per shard; misconfiguration could lead to increased OOM risk
Backpressure mis-tuning could cascade and surface as elevated 5xx rates in upstream services
Security-sensitive: mis-implementation of tenant auth could allow cross-tenant injection — security review required
comments: 2025-02-19 - Ava Chen: Kickoff meeting notes added. Confirmed primary goals and non-goals. Decided to favor CBOR over MessagePack due to canonical encoding and better support for typed maps.

2025-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Completed prototype of gRPC multiplexer and CBOR encoder. Local benchmarks show 2.8x size reduction and 1.6x CPU cost increase on small messages. Pushed prototype to branch feature/ingest-mesh-proto (PR #342)

2025-02-27 - Sofia Patel (SRE): Load-test run #1 with synthetic traffic (250k eps) exposed increased P95 latency during bursts. Root cause: token-bucket refill config too aggressive. Adjusted refill to 0.6x and re-ran with improved P95.
2025-03-01 - Security (review): Requested explicit threat model for cross-tenant auth; flagged that rehydration manifests must be KMS-encrypted. Marked security_review_required = true
2025-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented per-tenant LRU dedup cache with bounded memory; added metrics and a debug endpoint to inspect cache hit rate. Observed ~12% dedup rate on beta dataset.
2025-03-05 - QA: Created test matrix (preservation of correlation IDs, sampling correctness, retry semantics). Next: canary rollout checklist and alert thresholds defined
